tier_reason: Upgraded B to A on the HttpArena precedent (actix, cardigan, dusty, libxev, ntex): every quoted number matches site/data/results/helidon-tuned.json, helidon-production.json and the sibling nginx/userver/hical/drogon JSON files; the code is public (frameworks/helidon-tuned/{Dockerfile,pom.xml,src/main/java/com/httparena/*.java,src/main/resources/application.yaml}, frameworks/nginx/{Dockerfile,nginx.conf}, scripts/benchmark.sh, scripts/lib/profiles.sh), JDK and nginx build flags are in the Dockerfiles, and the CPU model (Threadripper PRO 3995WX) is in site/data/current.json.

corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX (Zen 2, 64 cores / 128 threads, one NUMA node), 251 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-22-generic, Docker 29.3.0 (runc), performance governor (HttpArena site/data/current.json and site/content/docs/hardware/_index.md). The server container is pinned to cpuset 0-31,64-95 (32 cores / 64 threads) and the load generator (gcannon for H/1.1, h2load for HTTP/2) to 32-63,96-127 over loopback; 5 s runs, best of 3 (scripts/lib/common.sh, scripts/lib/profiles.sh, scripts/benchmark.sh).
corrections.claimed_speedup: HttpArena (ratios derived from page data): baseline-h2-256 3,612,898 req/s (tuned) vs nginx 3,414,750 (1.06x), production variant 3,502,618 (1.03x); baseline-h2-1024 3,819,721 vs nginx 3,320,285 (1.15x), production 3,761,200 (1.13x); baseline-h2c (cleartext HTTP/2) 4,156,960 / 4,457,541 / 4,497,059 at 256 / 1024 / 4096 connections vs nginx 2,456,329 / 2,490,271 / 2,519,351 (1.69x to 1.79x); json-comp-4096 325,703 vs userver 297,311 (1.10x), proxygen-coro 262,212 (1.24x), hical 261,955 (1.24x), proxygen 243,887 (1.34x), Drogon 127,466 (2.56x), the top C/C++ rows on that profile (nginx, h2o, agensio and mongoose do not run it); pipelined-4096 (reference-only profile) 10,654,871 vs nginx 4,037,345 (2.64x), Drogon 7,801,404 (1.37x).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Helidon: Oracle JDK 27 image (container-registry.oracle.com/java/jdk-no-fee-term:27), Maven 3.9.16 package of Helidon SE 27.0.0, run as java -jar app.jar with default JVM options (frameworks/helidon-tuned/Dockerfile); the tuned variant turns off HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 request/response-header and path validation in application.yaml, the production variant keeps it. C/C++ rows: nginx 1.31.4 with a custom handler module, Debian trixie toolchain, --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG', linked against the system OpenSSL (the Dockerfile's quictls comment has no matching build step); h2o clang CMake Release -march=native -mtune=native (no LTO); userver CMake Release -march=native; hical gcc-14 CMake Release -march=native -mtune=native; proxygen CMake Release from a digest-pinned proxygen base image with mimalloc preloaded; Drogon CMake Release in the unpinned drogonframework/drogon:latest image with jemalloc preloaded (HttpArena frameworks/<name>/Dockerfile).
corrections.caveats: Narrow win. Against nginx, Helidon is ahead only on baseline-h2 (1.06x to 1.15x), baseline-h2c (1.69x to 1.79x) and the reference-only pipelined profile; it is behind nginx on baseline-4096 (0.52x), limited-conn-4096 (605,487 vs 2,626,297, 0.23x), json-tls-4096 (0.53x), json-h2c (1,087,863 vs 1,730,838, 0.63x), static-h2 (0.32x) and static-tls (0.45x). nginx's HTTP/2 path is the slowest C/C++ HTTP/2 stack on the board: at baseline-h2-256 h2o (16,106,978), agensio (14,744,015), proxygen (5,845,844) and proxygen-coro (5,185,268) are all ahead of Helidon (0.22x to 0.70x), and agensio and proxygen also lead on h2c. The json-comp win is over C++ frameworks only; Helidon gzips through java.util.zip GZIPOutputStream, which calls the JDK's native zlib, so compression is C code on both sides. The tuned entry disables header and path validation for the benchmark (the production variant keeps it and still edges nginx on h2). Both Helidon entries are maintained in HttpArena by Helidon developer tomas-langer, so they are vendor-tuned submissions run by the suite. Results files carry no dates; git history shows helidon-tuned.json last changed 2026-10-08/10 (Helidon 27.0.0 upgrade) and nginx.json 2026-08-30, so rows come from separate runs on the same machine. 5 s runs, best of 3, server limited to 32 of 64 cores. The Helidon README states no benchmark numbers.
corrections.why_faster: Not a Java language win and not established by the sources. The HTTP/2 lead is over nginx's comparatively slow HTTP/2 implementation (every other C/C++ HTTP/2 server on the board is faster than Helidon); the json-comp lead is over C++ framework JSON paths (Drogon's jsoncpp, folly::dynamic in proxygen), with gzip done by native zlib on both sides; the pipelined lead is nginx's pipelining cost. Helidon's Níma server runs one virtual thread per request on JDK 27 with the C2 JIT.

notes: All quoted numbers verified and tier raised to A on the HttpArena precedent (CPU model published in current.json). Shortcomings to record: beats nginx only on h2/h2c and the reference-only pipelined profile while losing 0.23x-0.64x on six other shared profiles; h2o, agensio, proxygen and proxygen-coro (C/C++) beat it on h2, the record's caveats omitted proxygen; json-comp win is over C++ frameworks with zlib on both sides; vendor-maintained tuned entry with validation off; cross-run rows (Oct vs Aug 2026). Metadata confirmed: Apache-2.0, 3.8k stars, last commit 2026-10-11, not a fork, not archived.

tier_reason: Well-known independent shootout (LesnyRumcajs/grpc_bench) with public harness code (rust_thruster_st_bench, rust_thruster_mt_bench, cpp_grpc_st_bench, cpp_grpc_mt_bench Dockerfiles and sources, bench.sh) and stated CPUs for both runs; held at B, as for grpc/grpc in wave 5, because the C++ side links Debian's prebuilt, unpinned libgrpc++ whose build flags and version are not stated by the harness.

corrections.claimed_speedup: grpc_bench complex_proto unary, ratios derived from page data. Latest run (discussion 559, 2026-04-23, commit c4c93b3): 1 server CPU rust_thruster_st 98,464 req/s and rust_thruster_mt 88,443 vs cpp_grpc_st 57,140, cpp_grpc_mt 57,403, cpp_asio_grpc 56,669 (st vs st 1.72x, mt vs mt 1.54x); 2 CPUs rust_thruster_mt 134,859 vs cpp_grpc_mt 74,574 (1.81x) and cpp_asio_grpc 74,869; 3 CPUs 138,576 vs 81,581 (1.70x); 4 CPUs 135,989 vs 85,485 (1.59x). Older run (wiki 2022-04-23, commit 14a8435): 1 CPU rust_thruster_st 41,334 (23.88 ms avg) vs cpp_grpc_st 26,700, cpp_grpc_mt 26,376, cpp_asio_grpc 24,926 (1.55x, 1.57x, 1.66x), rust_thruster_mt 36,793 (1.39x vs cpp_grpc_mt); at 2 CPUs rust_thruster_mt 56,740 vs cpp_grpc_mt 69,882 (0.81x) and at 3 CPUs 65,903 vs 71,806 (0.92x).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: 2026-04 run at c4c93b3: rust_thruster_st/mt on the rust:1.94 image, cargo build --release --locked with opt-level 3, codegen-units 1, lto true, jemallocator; thruster 1.3.10 (hyper_server feature) plus thruster-grpc 0.2.3 on hyper 0.14 and prost 0.11; st runs tokio current_thread, mt a multi-thread runtime with GRPC_SERVER_CPUS workers. cpp_grpc_st/mt on the gcc:15.2.0 image: g++ -O3 -flto (mt adds --std=c++20) on main.cpp and the generated stubs, linked against Debian's prebuilt libgrpc++-dev and jemalloc (apt-get, unpinned; Debian's grpc package is 1.51.1, search snippet only), so the -O3 -flto flags never reach the gRPC core. 2022 run at 14a8435: rust:1.59 with thruster 1.2.2, thruster-grpc from git and hyper 0.13, same release profile; C++ on gcc:11 with the then-current Debian libgrpc++-dev (version not checked). HEAD has since moved the C++ images to gcc:16.1.0.
corrections.hardware: 2026-04-23 run (discussion 559): Intel Xeon Gold 6548N @ 2.80 GHz (16 cores shown), 64 GB RAM; server limited to 1-4 CPUs and 4096m RAM, ghz client on 11 CPUs, 120 s with 30 s warmup, 50 connections, 1000 concurrency. 2022-04-23 run (wiki): Intel Xeon E5-1650 v3 @ 3.50 GHz, 32 GB RAM; server limited to 1, 2 or 3 CPUs and 512m RAM, client 9 CPUs.
corrections.workload: grpc_bench complex_proto unary SayHello echo: 50 client connections, 1000 concurrent requests, unlimited QPS, 120 s with 30 s warmup; server capped by docker --cpus at 1-4 CPUs (2026 run, 4096m RAM) or 1-3 CPUs (2022 run, 512m RAM).
corrections.caveats: The Thruster README gives no benchmark numbers, only 'Runs fast'. The measured server is thruster plus the separate thruster-rs/thruster-grpc crate on hyper's HTTP/2 stack and tokio, the same hyper/h2 base as tonic, so the result largely measures hyper/h2 rather than Thruster's own code. In the 2022 run the win was single-CPU only (cpp_grpc_mt led at 2 and 3 CPUs); the 2026 run shows rust_thruster_mt ahead of cpp_grpc_mt at 1-4 CPUs (1.54x to 1.81x), but java_vertx_grpc beats it at 2-4 CPUs and rust_tonic_st beats it at 1 CPU. The C++ baseline is Debian's distro libgrpc++ (1.51.1 per Debian's tracker, a December 2022 release; search snippet only), not an upstream gRPC built with the harness's -O3 -flto, so it is both older and built with distro flags. Server CPU limits use docker --cpus quotas, which penalise gRPC C++'s extra internal threads. Thruster's last commit is 2024-10-16 (stale).
corrections.why_faster: Runtime and library, not the Rust language: tokio with hyper's h2 crate and jemalloc against gRPC C++'s completion-queue server with its own internal threads under a docker CPU quota, with the C++ gRPC core taken from a distro package not built at the harness's -O3 -flto (inference from the benchmark setup; no source claim).

notes: Both runs verified; benchmark_url switched to the newer 2026-04-23 discussion, where thruster beats cpp_grpc_mt at 1-4 CPUs (1.54x-1.81x), while the 2022 wiki run shows a 1-CPU-only win. Shortcomings to record: C++ side is Debian's prebuilt libgrpc++ (old 1.51.1, distro flags, unpinned), so same_opt_level is false; Thruster's gRPC path is thruster-grpc on hyper/h2, overlapping tonic's stack; no first-party claim; repo stale. Metadata confirmed: MIT, 1.1k stars, last commit 2024-10-16, not a fork, not archived.

tier_reason: Upgraded B to A on the HttpArena precedent: every quoted number matches site/data/results/tokio-uring.json and the sibling nginx/drogon/hical/agensio/h2o/mongoose/libreactorng JSON files; the code is public (frameworks/tokio-uring/{Dockerfile,Cargo.toml,src/main.rs}, frameworks/nginx/{Dockerfile,nginx.conf}, scripts/benchmark.sh, scripts/lib/profiles.sh), Rust and nginx flags are in the Dockerfiles and Cargo.toml, and the CPU model (Threadripper PRO 3995WX) is in site/data/current.json.

corrections.hardware: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX (Zen 2, 64 cores / 128 threads, one NUMA node), 251 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-22-generic, Docker 29.3.0 (runc), performance governor (HttpArena site/data/current.json and site/content/docs/hardware/_index.md). The server container is pinned to cpuset 0-31,64-95 (32 cores / 64 threads) and the load generator (gcannon for H/1.1, h2load for HTTP/2) to 32-63,96-127 over loopback; 5 s runs, best of 3 (scripts/lib/common.sh, scripts/lib/profiles.sh, scripts/benchmark.sh).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: tokio-uring entry: rust:1.95 image, RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native' cargo build --release with opt-level 3, codegen-units 1, thin LTO, panic=abort, tokio-uring 0.5 (frameworks/tokio-uring/Dockerfile and Cargo.toml). C/C++ rows: nginx 1.31.4 with a custom handler module, Debian trixie toolchain, --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG'; h2o clang CMake Release -march=native -mtune=native (no LTO); mongoose gcc-14 -O3 -march=native -flto; Drogon CMake Release in the unpinned drogonframework/drogon:latest image with jemalloc preloaded; hical gcc-14 CMake Release -march=native -mtune=native; libreactorng -O3 -march=native (HttpArena frameworks/<name>/Dockerfile).
corrections.caveats: Not an io_uring win: the suite's plain tokio entry (epoll, same hand-rolled parser design, same Rust flags) is faster than tokio-uring on every shared profile (baseline-4096 4,187,085 vs 3,565,878; limited-conn-4096 2,721,455 vs 2,636,459; pipelined-4096 54,755,795 vs 48,876,057). The entry is a minimal hand-rolled server written for HttpArena (no maintainer listed, not the tokio-uring project's own code): it routes only /pipeline and answers every other path with the a+b sum, and sends about 63 bytes per response against about 135 for nginx (Date and Server headers; derived from page data, bandwidth over req/s), so the per-request work is not the same. At baseline-4096 it is behind libreactorng (4,377,377), libioma (4,255,834), mongoose (3,707,598) and h2o (3,641,609) and level with agensio; at limited-conn-4096 it ties nginx (1.00x) and is behind libioma, mongoose, libreactorng and h2o. The large pipelined ratio is on a reference-only profile (pipeline depth 16) and mostly reflects nginx's pipelining cost. 5 s runs, best of 3, server limited to 32 of 64 cores; results files are undated. The tokio-uring README states no benchmark numbers and calls the project 'still very young'; last commit 2025-07-07.
corrections.why_faster: Minimal handler and response, not Rust or io_uring: the HttpArena entry is a bare per-core server that emits about half the response bytes of nginx's custom module and skips routing, and the suite's epoll-based tokio entry of the same design is faster still, so io_uring is not the cause (frameworks/tokio-uring/src/main.rs, frameworks/tokio/meta.json, results JSON).

notes: All quoted numbers verified; tier raised to A on the HttpArena precedent. Shortcomings to record: the record's why_faster (io_uring) is contradicted by the suite's own epoll tokio entry, which beats tokio-uring 1.17x at baseline-4096; minimal hand-rolled handler sending about half nginx's response bytes (same_algorithm false); behind four C servers at baseline and limited-conn; pipelined is reference-only. Metadata confirmed: MIT, 1.5k stars, last commit 2025-07-07 (stale), not a fork, not archived.
